To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PROPRAPHOS is an effective catalyst for the hydrogenation of dehydropetide esters with a high enantioselectivity, and (2) the configuration of the chiral carbon atom in the dehydroamino acid ester substrate affects the catalytic asymmetric hydrogenation.

the cationic Rh(I) complex of the chiral diphosphanes PROPHOS or BPPM is a highly efficient catalyst for the hydrogenation of the dehydrodipeptides bearing a fluorine substituent at the aromatic ring of the substrate.

the cationic complexes of rhodium with diphosphine PROPHOS and BPPFM were found to be efficient catalysts for asymmetric hydrogenation of dehydrated dipeptides bearing different protective groups and that the chiral centers in the substrate had significant effect on the catalytic induction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and the catalytic asymmetric hydrogenation of dehydroripeptide esters, which is a new class of substrates for the asymmetric hydrogenation.
the development of new catalytic asymmetric hydrogenation methods for the synthesis of chiral dehydrodipeptides and dipeptides.
the development of new chiral diphos-phines and their rhodium complexes for the catalytic asymmetric hydrogenation of prochiral olefins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hydrogenation of N-[(Z)-2-fluorobenzylidenepyruvate]- (R)-phenylalaninyl ester using the rhodium complex of the chiral diphosphate ligand (R,R)-PROPRAPHOS in the presence of 2 equiv. of triethylamine gave the corresponding dipeptides with an ee value of 53% in 98% yield.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hydrogenation of dehydroripeptide derivatives with the (Z)-configuration of the C=N bond is an excellent model system to study the influence of the chiral ligand on the asymmetric induction and the role of the substrate on the stereoselectivity.
the best results were obtained when the chiral center of the substrate is in the α-position and the protecting groups are Boc or Bn.
the best results are obtained when a chiral center is present in the dehydrodipeptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a chiral center in a substrate bearing a chiral ligand in the catalytic system is a powerful way to increase the enantioselectivity of the reaction.
PROPRAPHOS can be used in the hydrogenation of deproteinated substrates, but BPPM is more efficient in the case of substrates with Boc protection.

the hydrogenation of the dehydrodipeptides is not only a good method for the synthesis of the corresponding dipeptides but it is also a good method for determining the enantioselectivity of the chiral diphosphate ligand.
